headline: The parts are here.
The
fields aren't.
hero.lede: An independent review of federalfp.com for the E-Commerce Developer & Content Editor role. I read three of the nine sitemap files (54,496 URLs), five category pages, 19 product pages and eight content pages, plus five pages on the sister store patriothyd.com — no logins, no carts. Search by part number works and the structured data is better than most distributors ship. The catalog behind it shows the marks of a bulk ERP import that nobody has mapped yet: 20,242 product URLs with no URL key, specs trapped inside title strings, prices printed on parts you can only request a quote for, and supplier logos standing in for photos on 69% of the catalog. Six findings, five working fixes — each one is the job.

why.title: Why Federal Fluid Power
why.sub: The posting is a catalog job first: product listings, attributes, images, the ERP-to-Magento sync. A 52,000-SKU distributor's storefront shows exactly how that sync is doing, so I read it before applying.
rows: Findings 2, 4 and 5 — attributes, imagery, titles and descriptions.
Findings 1 and 3 — URL keys and the price/stock signals an import leaves behind.
Keep product and inventory data accurate
The attribute parser and option normalizer below are the tools I would run first.
Finding 6 — the Patriot Hydraulics strings on Federal's pages.
why.note: Everything here comes from public pages: served HTML, the sitemaps, robots.txt and JSON-LD. I did not log in, add to cart or submit a quote request. Numbers marked “sitemap-wide” come from the three sitemap files I fetched, not all nine.

strengths.title: Part-number search works
strengths.text: Searching FI-TE-04LLMK-W3-MS returns exactly one hit with price and Add to Cart, and the results page is noindex with a canonical to the search root — the right handling for buyers who type manufacturer codes.

strengths.title: Structured data most distributors never ship
strengths.text: Every sampled product page carries Product + Offer with price, currency and availability, shippingDetails (2–5 business days, $9.99, US), a merchant return policy and a BreadcrumbList; category pages add an OfferCatalog. 19 of 19.

strengths.title: The Engineering Toolbox is real content
strengths.text: /engineering-toolbox/ is a 2,570-word in-browser calculator suite — cylinder force, speed and flow, rod buckling, pumps, HPUs, pneumatics, conversions — with Shop Cylinders links back into the catalog, alongside a hose configurator and a product configurator.

findings.title: 37% of sitemap product URLs have no URL key and are blocked by robots.txt
findings.count: 20,242 of 54,496 URLs (37.1%) across the three sitemap files fetched · 3 of 3 sampled pages return 200 with a robots-blocked canonical
findings.observed: robots.txt disallows /catalog/product/view/, yet sitemap_005.xml lists 10,879 URLs and sitemap_009.xml 9,363 of the form /catalog/product/view/id/93633/ — products imported without a url_key. Fetching three of them returns 200, and each page's own canonical points at another blocked URL (/catalog/product/view/_ignore_category/1/id/101454/s/804500106/). Google receives twenty thousand URLs it is told not to crawl.
findings.why: The role owns ERP-to-Magento product data, and a missing url_key on ~20,000 SKUs is exactly the kind of import-mapping gap that silently removes products from search.
findings.fix: Filter the product grid for URL Key = empty, bulk-update (or re-import a CSV) with url_key = slugified name + SKU, reindex catalog_url_rewrite, regenerate the sitemap and verify no /catalog/product/view/ URLs remain. Keep the Disallow so the numeric duplicates never index.

findings.title: Specs live inside the title string; where attributes exist the values are dirty
findings.count: 18 of 19 PDPs with only Name / SKU / Weight / Brand · 0 of 19 with a thread, port, material or pressure attribute · Cylinders: 6 of 17 Bore values are inch-mark twins, 72 of 142 Bore×Stroke values are x/X twins, 2 values are Excel date serials
findings.observed: The More Information table on 18 of 19 sampled PDPs is Product Name, SKU, Weight and Brand; thread size, port, material and pressure appear only inside the name, e.g. “BV3-04-NPT 1/4″ Three way selector Ball valve w/ 1/4″ NPT Threads (5,800 PSI).” Where spec attributes exist (Cylinders, 953 items) the filter values are unnormalized: Bore lists 2.5 and 2.5″, Stroke 8 and 8″, Bore×Stroke 2 1/2 x 10 and 2 1/2 X 10, Rod Diameter 1 1/4″ and 1.25, Column Load mixes 11520 lbs with a bare 11. Two values are date serials — Ports (NPTF) = 44628 and Rod Diameter = 44624 — the sign of a fraction like 3/8 converted to a date in a spreadsheet before import. Weights are round defaults (a $3.40 stud coupling weighs 10.000000).
findings.why: “Keep product data accurate” and “build listings with attributes” is the core of this role; these are the errors a buyer hits when filtering.
findings.fix: Define thread_size, port_size, material, pressure_rating, pack_qty and mfr_part_number in an attribute set per product line; parse them out of existing names with a one-off script (the parser below is that script); normalize option values — strip inch marks, lowercase x, one unit convention — under Manage Options; re-export the cylinder CSV with text-formatted columns so 3/8 never becomes 44628 again.

findings.title: Price and availability contradict each other — the public symptoms of an unmapped ERP sync
findings.count: 9 of 19 PDPs are Request-Pricing-only, and 8 of those 9 declare InStock in schema · 1 of 19 prints $0.00 · Chairs & Creepers page 1: 20 of 20 unpriced · a $40,000–$50,000 price bucket on couplings
findings.observed: Unavailable items swap Add to Cart for a Request Pricing and Availability button but still print a price on the PDP ($3.40 on a stud coupling whose listing card hides the price), and their JSON-LD still declares availability InStock. Product 804500106 shows $0.00. No PDP shows a stock quantity or in/out-of-stock text; only the three Patriot-brand valves show a lead time (“Usually Ships Within 1–3 Days”). Whole leaf categories are unpriced, and the Couplings price facet offers a $40,000–$50,000 bucket, so at least one coupling is priced above $40,000.
findings.why: The posting names the Magento-ERP integration and inventory accuracy; these are what a buyer, and Google, see when quantity and price fields do not map cleanly.
findings.fix: Map ERP quantity and price into qty, is_in_stock and price on every sync run and key the RFQ module off is_salable; render Magento's stock-status block on PDPs; set Offer availability to OutOfStock or BackOrder (or drop the Offer) when the button is RFQ; add a sync alert for price = 0 or price > $10,000 on fittings.

findings.title: Manufacturer logos stand in for product photos on tens of thousands of SKUs
findings.count: 10 of 19 sampled PDPs show a supplier logo as the only image · sitemap-wide, 35,744 of 51,918 products (69%) share a generic first image · 512 have no image at all
findings.observed: Five Yuken items show alaindustries.jpg, others show dnpamerica.jpg, stucchi.jpg, poclain.jpg or Damanlogo.jpg as the product picture; the two Stauff couplings share one family drawing. In the sitemaps the first image is a file shared by 100 or more products for 35,744 of 51,918 products, and one of six logo files for 14,732. Homepage category tiles carry mismatched alt text (Fittings.png alt=“Hydraulic Oil”).
findings.why: The role writes copy, attributes and images for the store; a logo where the part should be is the single most visible content gap for a buyer comparing fittings.
findings.fix: Pull supplier line-drawing and CAD sets (Stauff, Tompkins and Poclain publish them) and import by SKU via Import → Products with base_image, small_image and thumbnail; use a per-family drawing as the fallback instead of the logo; set a Magento image placeholder so the 512 image-less SKUs stop rendering blank; fix the tile alts.

findings.title: One meta description sitewide, code-only titles, and three URL layers for the same part
findings.count: 19 of 19 PDPs + 7 of 7 content pages share one description · 11 of 19 titles are the bare part code · 12 of 17 sitemap product URLs return 200 with a different canonical · 2,368 of 2,515 category URLs (94%) end in -1/-2/-3 · 58 homepage links into an alias category tree
findings.observed: Every product and content page fetched carries the same description (“Discover a trusted online destination for all your hydraulic requirements…”); product titles are the bare part code with no brand or site suffix (“BV3-04-NPT”). The URL layer is duplicated three ways: sitemap product URLs that canonical elsewhere (one to another SKU's key), category-path product links on listings whose canonical is the root URL, and a /hydraulics-1/ alias tree the homepage links into 58 times. Each page emits two BreadcrumbList blocks.
findings.why: “Content editor” for a 52,000-SKU catalog means templates, not hand edits, and the crawl budget is currently spent on duplicates of the same part.
findings.fix: Set product meta templates under Product Fields Auto-Generation ({{name}} | {{brand}} hydraulic {{category}} | Federal Fluid Power, and a description from name + brand + first spec); set Use Categories Path for Product URLs to No with permanent redirects on key change; run a URL-rewrite cleanup so old keys 301 instead of 200; relink the homepage grid to canonical category URLs; remove the second breadcrumb block from the Hyvä template.

findings.title: Federal's pages carry Patriot Hydraulics' copyright and phone number; policy links go to the wrong pages
findings.count: 2 wrong-brand strings on every page · Shipping and Return Policy both link to /terms/ · 2 “#” footer links · 6 test/junk pages in the sitemap · the same typo on 19 of 19 PDPs · 2 of 2 SKUs duplicated across both domains
findings.observed: federalfp.com's footer reads “© 2023 Patriot Hydraulics” and the header says Call Us 734-479-9641 — Patriot's number (Federal's is 734-455-1722). Shipping Policy and Return Policy both open the 2,320-word terms page, and a second copy of it exists at /ffp-terms-conditions-of-sale/. Order History and Order Tracking link to #. The sitemap lists /test/, /webkul/, /webkul-seller/, /pictures/ and /privacy-patriothyd/; the 404 page is a clone of the homepage with the homepage title; every PDP prints “ask about our leads times?” Both sampled SKUs exist on patriothyd.com with identical content and self-referencing canonicals on each domain.
findings.why: These are the first things a customer sees, and each is a ten-minute fix inside Content → Blocks and Pages for someone who owns the multi-store setup.
findings.fix: Scope the footer and header blocks to the Federal store view (copyright, phone); create real Shipping and Returns pages and relink the footer; disable the test pages and drop them from the sitemap; assign a proper no-route page; fix the typo in the PDP template; choose one canonical domain per SKU or noindex the Patriot copies.

also: Descriptions: 17 of 19 sampled PDPs under 50 words; 7 of 19 just repeat the name.
Datasheets: 5 of 19 PDPs have Amasty attachments (Poclain MS11: PDF + DXF + STP); none link a PDF otherwise.
Category tree: 2,515 category URLs in one sitemap file, seven levels deep; no empty category found; Couplings alone is 4,114 items over 206 pages.
No sort control renders on any listing (the toolbar is Show 20 / 40 / 80 only); Couplings filters are Category, Brand and Price — no thread size, port or material.

Page weight: product pages are 504–511 KB of HTML with 68–69 script tags; the search results page is 1.74 MB because a 528-value cross-reference facet renders inline; every page embeds a 250-option country list for the quote modal.
Homepage: 21 h1 elements (each category tile is one), no social links, favicon is a JPEG, no og:image.
Patriot's sitemap index has 14 files to Federal's 9; product lastmod dates cluster in Aug 2026 (48,233) and Sep 2026 (3,749), consistent with a full-catalog resync.

prototypes.title: URL-key generator
prototypes.what: Takes the real sampled products with no URL key and produces the url_key Magento would need, as the CSV the bulk import takes.

prototypes.title: Attribute parser
prototypes.what: Paste any product name from the catalog and watch thread size, port, pressure, material and pack quantity fall into structured attributes — the script that populates the attribute set.

prototypes.title: Option normalizer
prototypes.what: The Cylinders filter values as they are, and as they come out of one normalization pass: inch marks stripped, x lowercased, fractions restored from date serials.

prototypes.title: Stock and price, in agreement
prototypes.what: The nine Request-Pricing products with their current price and InStock schema, and the corrected Offer each should emit.

prototypes.title: Meta template preview
prototypes.what: The 19 sampled products run through one title and description template — every page unique, every one under 60 and 155 characters.

prototypes.title: Store-view footer
prototypes.what: The footer as it renders on federalfp.com today and as it would with store-view-scoped blocks.
